narrative_markdown:
## Overview
Today feels about the same as yesterday temperature-wise, though surface winds will be calmer, with rain expected again today, as it rained yesterday too. Warm morning sun will give way to afternoon cloud development, leading to isolated evening thunderstorms across the Nyanza Basin.

## Today's Forecast
Daytime maximum temperatures will reach 29°C / 19°C (84°F / 66°F) for overnight lows. Isolated evening thunderstorms are expected to develop around 16:00 to 19:00 EAT, bringing an estimated 3.7 mm (0.15 in) of precipitation. Surface winds over land will peak around 17 km/h (9 kt) from the SW, though lake breezes will build stronger localized flow in coastal areas. The peak UV index will reach 8.9 (Very High), requiring UV protection during midday hours (10:00 to 15:00 EAT). Air quality based on CAMS model output indicates an AQI of 93 (Moderate); local ground sensors at Kisumu Airport, Ochieng' Avenue, and Dunga Beach are currently reporting stale data (>3 hours old) without numeric AQI readings.

## Extended Outlook
Days 1 to 3 (Aug 20 – Aug 22): Near-term confidence is moderate-to-high, backed by ECMWF's excellent Day+3 rain verification track record (100%). Expect daytime highs ranging from 29°C / 84°F to 30°C / 86°F and overnight lows around 18°C / 64°F. Scattered evening showers persist on Thursday, Aug 20 (3.1 mm / 0.12 in), followed by drier conditions on Friday, Aug 21 (0.0 mm) and Saturday, Aug 22 (0.9 mm / 0.04 in).

Days 4 to 7 (Aug 23 – Aug 26): Lower-confidence extended guidance draws on ECMWF Day+7 tracking. Rain chances return on Sunday, Aug 23 with heavier convective showers totaling 5.6 mm (0.22 in), continuing with intermittent shower activity on Monday, Aug 24 (3.7 mm / 0.15 in) and Wednesday, Aug 26 (4.8 mm / 0.19 in). Temperatures remain steady between 28°C / 82°F and 29°C / 84°F. Note that extended outlook forecasts provide day-level totals only, as hourly onset timing is unavailable at this lead time.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
Localized lightning hazards and sudden wind gusts during late afternoon convective cells. Midday UV index peaking at 8.9 (Very High) poses elevated burn risk. Moderate air quality (AQI 93) may cause minor discomfort for sensitive respiratory groups.

## Lake Victoria — Conditions for Boaters
Early morning light winds over the lake will shift to south-southeasterly and intensify by mid-afternoon to 23 km/h (12 kt) to 29 km/h (16 kt). Peak gusts over open water will reach up to 35 km/h (19 kt). Wave height will build during late afternoon hours alongside developing convective clouds. Boaters should exercise caution after 15:00 EAT due to potential squalls and isolated thunderstorms over eastern lake waters.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
Mean sea-level pressure across the Nyanza Basin remains steady near 1014.4 hPa, with a typical diurnal thermal troughing dip toward 1011.5 hPa by mid-afternoon. Across the 24–72 hour synoptic window, pressure monitoring points remain stable (ranging from 1014.2 hPa at Busia to 1016.7 hPa in the high-elevation Kericho sector), sustaining moist onshore breeze convergence from Lake Victoria into the surrounding lowlands. Daytime solar heating interacting with low-level moisture transport will drive moderate instability (CAPE reaching 1000–1500 J/kg in multi-model blend), initiating evening convective cells.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
Forecaster confidence for today's forecast is elevated by heavily weighting ECMWF for precipitation timing and ICON for wind speeds. ECMWF maintains a 100% rain accuracy record at Day+3, while ICON leads near-term surface wind verification with an average error under 10 km/h. GFS continues a systematic overestimation of surface winds by over 20 km/h, requiring manual downscaling. Local ground AQI stations at Kisumu Airport (A418534), Ochieng' Avenue (A418300), and Dunga Beach (A418504) carry stale readings (4 to 27 hours old), so CAMS reanalysis was used exclusively for current air quality assessment.
